sections.heading: 1. Build steadier ankles

② Once easy, do the same on one leg.

④ Easy? Try eyes closed; 1–2 min a day.

caption:
Two sprains later, Momo's ankles feel wobbly on bushwalks and the sand. Even once pain has gone, ankles can lose some strength and some sense of where they are.

Clinical Pilates can work on both: reformer footwork for calf and foot strength, slow heel raises over three to four seconds for control, and balance drills that get progressively harder.

Try this today: stand on one leg near a bench for 30 seconds, then try it with eyes closed if that's easy. A minute or two a day is a good start.

An ankle that keeps giving way, recurring swelling or pain taking weight are worth a physio assessment. Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physio can tailor a program. Book online via the link in bio.
